title: Security posture discovery with Evora Health
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 summary
Share diagram of VPC private deployment options and network flow
Schedule SE-led technical deep dive to run sample benchmark (30-60 min)
Provide draft MSA and security addendum for legal review
action_items: Alex Chen: Send SOC2/ISO docs + security whitepaper by 2026-07-09
Morgan Lee: Prepare benchmark plan and list of sample queries; schedule deep dive with Ravi and Leah by 2026-07-14
Marta Silva (Evora): Share internal DFIR requirements and legal milestones by 2026-07-10
meeting_header: Date: 2026-07-07 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood), Morgan Lee (Redwood), Priya Kaur (Redwood), Dana Ortiz (Evora - CISO), Ravi Singh (Evora - Head of Platform), Leah Brooks (Evora - DevOps), Marta Silva (Evora - Legal)
summary: Introductory security posture discovery. Evora is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) for PHI-adjacent workloads. Key concerns: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, RBAC and tenant isolation, audit logs and SIEM integration, encryption and BYOK/KMS/HSM, retention and deletion policy. Redwood to send compliance artifacts and schedule technical benchmark and legal follow-up.
topics: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 status
RBAC, tenant isolation, and least-privilege controls
Audit logs, retention, and SIEM export (CloudWatch/Splunk/Datadog)
Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/BYOK, HSM support
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through Evora's security questions around infra choices - hosted, dedicated, private. I'm Alex, AE, and with me is Morgan and Priya from our security/solutions team.
[00:14] Dana (Evora - CISO): Thanks Alex. We're looking at Redwood because we need predictable inference for PHI-adjacent workflows. Main asks: compliance evidence, SSO/SAML, key management (BYOK), and auditability.
[00:30] Morgan (Redwood SE): Great. Quick high level: Redwood offers hosted API with SOC2 Type II, Dedicated which gives reserved GPU pools + isolation, and Private which is VPC or on-prem for full network control. For encryption we support TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest with customer KMS integration.
[00:50] Ravi (Evora): Two quick clarifications - BYOK via customer-managed KMS? HSM? And how do you rotate keys?
[01:05] Priya (Redwood): Yes, BYOK supported - you can bring keys in cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and in Private deployments we support HSM-backed keys; rotation is customer-controlled and we store only metadata, not key material for BYOK. Key rotation cycles follow KMS policies; we can document lifecycle.
[01:30] Leah (Evora - DevOps): For audit logs - we need full request/response metadata (no PHI payloads) and ability to forward logs to Splunk. Retention is 7 years for some datasets; can Redwood export logs and provide tamper-evidence?
[01:50] Morgan (Redwood SE): We have structured audit logs: request IDs, model version, latencies, auth principal, and IPs. We can stream logs to customer SIEM via secure forwarder (syslog/HTTPS). Tamper-evidence: audit logs are immutably stored and we provide SHA hashes and time-based snapshots, plus exportable log bundles for forensics. We'll need to follow up with exact retention/archival process.
[02:15] Dana: Do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO? Also do you do pen tests and external attestations?
[02:30] Alex: We are SOC 2 Type II audited; ISO 27001 scope available for customers on enterprise plans, and we run annual pen tests and third-party assessments. I'll send the reports.
[02:45] Marta (Evora - Legal): Legal will want an artifacts pack - SOC2, ISO, penetration test summary, data processing addendum, and security addendum language. Can you share a draft?
[03:00] Alex: Absolutely - we'll share the draft MSA and security addendum and the compliance pack.
[03:10] Ravi: On RBAC - we need fine-grained roles mapping to our Okta groups, with scoped permissions (deploy, admin, read-only, audit). SCIM provisioning would help.
[03:30] Priya: We support SSO via SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning for groups. Roles map to policies in the console; for Dedicated/Private you can enforce stricter IAM and VPC-level controls.
[03:50] Leah: Does Redwood support tenant isolation? We prefer logical isolation for hosted but ultimately may require dedicated pools if isolation is absolute requirement.
[04:05] Morgan: Hosted is multi-tenant with strict containerization and workload isolation; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with tenancy guarantee; Private gives you VPC or on-premise where you're the sole tenant. We'll outline the differences in a table when we send docs.
[04:30] Dana: Data retention and deletion - can you guarantee deletion of customer data on request? We need ability to purge or set retention windows and get attestation.
[04:45] Priya: Yes - we offer configurable data retention policies. For hosted we retain minimal short-term caches (KV caches) for performance, configurable to zero for regulated customers, and we provide deletion attestations. For Private, deletion is under customer's control.
[05:10] Dana: For PHI-adjacent, we need network controls - can we run in our VPC and restrict egress?
[05:22] Morgan: Private VPC deployment supports customer-managed networking, egress rules, and we can enable VPC endpoints to avoid internet egress. Dedicated also supports VPC peering options for enterprise customers.
[05:40] Ravi: Any encryption-in-use when model weights are loaded to GPUs? We're concerned about memory scraping or snapshotting.
[05:55] Priya: For Dedicated and Private, we can enable encrypted caching and work with kernel-level protections; we also support secure enclave options for certain hardware. We'll need to align on threat model for the deep dive.
[06:20] Dana: Logging of request payloads - we must avoid storing PHI. Can Redwood redact or not persist raw prompts?
[06:35] Alex: By default we do not store full payloads for hosted unless configured; we offer options: store redacted metadata only, ephemeral caching, or no persistence. For compliance we can set prompt persistence to zero and enable request-level hashing for traceability without storing content.
[07:00] Leah: What about eDiscovery and legal hold? If a subpoena arrives, what's your support model?
[07:12] Alex: We provide log bundles and assist through legal channels; for hosted customers we can export relevant logs and metadata; for Private, you're in control. We'll include our legal process doc in the send.
[07:30] Marta: SLA and uptime for Dedicated vs Hosted - we'll need clarity for contractual language.
[07:40] Morgan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has our standard SLA. We'll include SLA PDFs and the different tiers.
[08:00] (crosstalk) Speaker 1: uh-huh, yeah
[08:20] Dana: For identity - we use Okta. Does Redwood support Just-in-Time provisioning? SCIM is important.
[08:35] Priya: Yes, Okta via SAML + SCIM; we support group sync and JIT provisioning paths. We'll share our SSO configuration guide.
[09:00] Ravi: Network egress and data residency - Evora must keep data in the US East region. Do you guarantee region-specific hosting?
[09:15] Alex: We have regional deployments; for hosted we can pin tenancy to specific regions, and Dedicated/Private naturally run in the customer-preferred region. We'll include region availability matrix.
[09:40] Leah: Any support for customer-managed audit log retention longer than 90 days? We need 7 years for certain tables.
[09:55] Morgan: We can stream logs to your SIEM and retain as long as you like on your side. On Redwood side, retention varies by plan but for enterprise we support extended retention and archiving.
[10:10] Dana: Pen testing cadence - do you share findings or only summaries?
[10:20] Alex: We share high-level summaries and remediation evidence; for NDAs we can share deeper reports under an NDA.
[10:30] Ravi: So action items: send SOC2 + ISO, SSO guide, VPC diagram, and a proposed benchmark. Also legal draft MSA.
[10:45] Alex: Correct. We'll also propose a short technical deep dive to run sample inference tests with your payloads to measure latency and token budgets.
[11:00] Dana: Timeline - we're aiming for vendor selection by end of July if possible; pilot in August.
[11:14] Morgan: That aligns. We'll aim to get docs and schedule the deep dive within a week.
[11:30] (brief pause)
[11:45] Leah: One more question - audit log integrity: is there an API for log queries and export, or is it only bulk exports?
[12:00] Priya: Both - we have APIs for query and real-time streaming; bulk exports are available for forensics. We'll include example endpoints.
[12:18] Dana: Anything around SIEM field mapping? We need to ensure fields like user_principal, model_version, request_id, and redaction flags are present.
[12:30] Morgan: We'll include a field mapping doc for Splunk/Datadog/S3 exports.
[12:45] (noise in background)
[13:00] Marta: On the legal doc, we will want indemnity language and data processing details. Also need to confirm export and deletion SLA.
[13:12] Alex: We'll prepare language and push to you; note that for enterprise plans we can negotiate DPAs and indemnities.
[13:25] Ravi: Regarding Dedicated latency/cost tradeoff - can you share typical P95 latencies for small prompt workloads vs quantized models?
[13:40] Morgan: Yes - we'll include performance numbers in the benchmark doc; typical P95 for gen small models on dedicated is sub-300ms for short prompts, depending on batching and kernel optimizations. For quantized models the memory savings reduce cost at small latency uplift. We'll provide a chart.
[14:05] Dana: Any certifications for supply chain or subprocessor lists?
[14:15] Alex: We maintain a subprocessors list and can provide it; supply chain details and subcontractor SOCs where applicable.
[14:30] Leah: For on-prem/private deployment, how long does provisioning take?
[14:40] Priya: Typical timelines: VPC deployment can be spun up in days with templates; on-prem installations are project-based (2-6 weeks) depending on hardware procurement and network approvals.
[14:58] Dana: Ok good. I think that's it on questions. Let's recap next steps.
[15:10] Alex: Recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO, SSO guide + SCIM config, VPC/private deployment diagram, benchmark plan, and draft MSA/security addendum. We'll schedule the SE deep dive next week.
[15:25] Marta: We'll review and send legal redlines - target to have comments by 2026-07-10.
[15:35] Dana: Thanks everyone.
[15:40] Alex: Thanks team, we'll follow up via email with attachments and calendar invites. End call.
[54:55] (call ended)
notes: Transcription has occasional misrecognized words (e.g., kernel optimizations noted as 'kernel options')
Customer is PHI-adjacent and requires long retention/strict deletion policies
AE + SE present; clear next steps and timeline for vendor selection
